answer.rationale: Rated against the objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue), not against general usefulness. memory_57 (5) is the only entry that names the target metric directly — qualified revenue — and also reports a guardrail check on retention, so it speaks to both the revenue and the sustainability halves of the objective. memory_44 (4) measures pipeline QUALITY, one step from qualified revenue, and is segment-scoped (enterprise); it omits close rates, CAC of sales-assist, and any durability window, so not a 5. memory_31 (3) and memory_86 (3) are mid: both are activation/completion proxies rather than revenue, but each carries a partial durability signal ('durable lift'; 'time-to-value' and 'early adoption'), and both sit upstream of revenue in a plausible chain. memory_73 (2) reports revenue but is the weakest kind of revenue evidence for THIS objective: promotional pricing lift is measured at acquisition, with no margin, no discount-cohort retention, no post-promotion renewal, and no time horizon — exactly the omissions that separate short-term revenue from sustainable revenue. It is also the memory the current competitor-pricing pressure will most tempt me to over-read; its acquisition lift was observed in a pre-competitor market and may not transfer to a price war. memory_91 (2) is rated least supported: it measures only week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' — a pure leading-indicator proxy with no revenue figure, no retention or expansion follow-through, and the shortest observation window of any entry. Tie-break against memory_73: memory_73 at least observed a revenue number, however fragile; memory_91 never touches revenue or durability at all, so as EVIDENCE for the stated objective it is the thinnest. Two cross-cutting caveats on the whole set: (1) every source is archived, so none of these can be re-audited for effect size, sample, or whether lifts persisted past the measurement window; (2) all six were consolidated on days 12-61 under different market conditions than day 76 — the competitor entry is a regime change that specifically undermines the pricing and SMB-acquisition memories. The current dips (activation -6%, onboarding -4%) point at the memory_31/86/91 cluster, but those are the proxy-only memories; if the single slot is spent there, the design should carry a revenue/retention readout so the next cycle inherits something rated higher than a 3.
